title: General Inclusion-Exclusion for k Sets
description: Proves the general inclusion-exclusion formula for k finite sets using Mathlib's Finset.inclusion_exclusion_card_biUnion. Establishes the inductive step (adding one more set to a union), the complementary counting form, explicit 2/3/4-set specializations, and the first Bonferroni inequality (union bound). 13 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-verified using Mathlib's Finset.inclusion_exclusion_card_biUnion and standard Finset lemmas.
originalContributions: general_inclusion_exclusion: wraps Mathlib's alternating-sum formula as a clean theorem
card_biUnion_insert: inductive step — |⋃_{i∈insert j s} Sᵢ| = |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| + |Sⱼ| - |⋃_{i∈s}(Sᵢ ∩ Sⱼ)|
biUnion_inter_right: distributivity of ∩ over ⋃ — (⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ) ∩ B = ⋃_{i∈s}(Sᵢ ∩ B)
union_bound: first Bonferroni inequality — |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| ≤ Σ_{i∈s} |Sᵢ|
four_set_inclusion_exclusion: explicit 4-set IE formula built by composing the 3-set and 2-set cases
card_sdiff_biUnion_int: complementary counting — |U \ ⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| = |U| - |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| (in ℤ)

overview.historicalContext: The general form of the inclusion-exclusion principle was developed independently by Daniel da Silva (1854) and Joseph Sylvester (1883). For a family of n finite sets {A₁,...,Aₙ}, the cardinality of their union follows the alternating sum: |⋃ᵢ Aᵢ| = Σ|Aᵢ| - Σ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ| + Σ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ∩Aₖ| - ... This extends the two-set formula (|A∪B| = |A|+|B|-|A∩B|) to arbitrary finite families. The complementary form — counting elements in a universe that avoid all 'bad' sets — is the foundation of sieve methods in number theory, from the Sieve of Eratosthenes to the large sieve. The Bonferroni inequalities (1936) give one-sided truncations of the IE formula, essential in probability theory (union bound = first Bonferroni inequality). Mathlib 4 formalizes the general formula in Combinatorics.Enumerative.InclusionExclusion via Finset.inclusion_exclusion_card_biUnion.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the general inclusion-exclusion principle for k finite sets: |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| = Σ_{∅≠t⊆s} (-1)^(|t|+1) |⋂_{i∈t} Sᵢ|. Also prove the inductive characterization (adding one set), the complementary counting form, and the first Bonferroni inequality.
overview.text: The proof has eight parts. Part I wraps Mathlib's `inclusion_exclusion_card_biUnion` into a clean statement. Part II establishes the key inductive step: distributing ∩ over ⋃ (biUnion_inter_right) enables reducing |⋃_{i∈insert j s} Sᵢ| to |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| + |Sⱼ| - |⋃_{i∈s}(Sᵢ∩Sⱼ)|. Part III handles base cases (empty and singleton index sets). Part IV specializes the general formula to two and three sets. Part V proves the Bonferroni union bound by induction: |S_a ∪ ⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| ≤ |S_a| + Σ_{i∈s}|Sᵢ|. Part VI covers complementary counting. Part VII proves the explicit four-set IE formula by composing the two-set and three-set cases.
overview.proofStrategy: The main theorem (general_inclusion_exclusion) is a one-line application of Mathlib's result. The inductive step (card_biUnion_insert) uses biUnion_inter_right to distribute intersection, then card_union_step and linarith. The three-set formula needs three distributivity steps: (A∪B)∩C=(A∩C)∪(B∩C), each proved by ext+simp+tauto. The four-set formula chains the three-set and two-set formulas with further intersection distributivity steps, closed by linarith. The union bound uses biUnion induction with card_union_le at each step.
keyInsights: Mathlib provides inclusion_exclusion_card_biUnion — the general formula is not new work, but the file makes it accessible and provides derived forms (inductive step, complementary, Bonferroni) that are harder to use directly from Mathlib.

biUnion_inter_right (distributivity of ∩ over ⋃) is the key enabling lemma: it converts a question about (⋃ Sᵢ) ∩ B into questions about each Sᵢ ∩ B separately, which is the heart of the inductive proof.
Working in ℤ (not ℕ) for cardinality formulas avoids natural-number underflow: intermediate steps can have negative values, and omega closes all arithmetic goals uniformly.

The four-set formula is proved by composition, not by hand: the two-set and three-set lemmas combine via distributivity, avoiding the error-prone manual alternating sum. This pattern generalizes to any fixed k.

The union bound (Bonferroni first inequality) is the most practically important result: it says you never overcount by ignoring intersections. Proved by induction using only card_union_le at each step.

conclusion.summary: Machine-verified general inclusion-exclusion for k finite sets: alternating sum over the powerset of the index set, inductive characterization, complementary counting, explicit 2/3/4-set formulas, and the Bonferroni union bound. 13 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms, 276 lines.
conclusion.implications: This formalization completes the structural picture of inclusion-exclusion: Mathlib provides the raw alternating sum, and this file adds the inductive step, complementary counting form, and Bonferroni inequality that are needed in practice. The biUnion_inter_right distributivity lemma and card_biUnion_insert inductive step are building blocks for more advanced sieve-method formalizations.
openQuestions: Formalize Möbius inversion as a consequence of general IE: if f(n) = Σ_{d|n} g(d), then g(n) = Σ_{d|n} μ(d)f(n/d), connecting the IE alternating sum to the Möbius function on the divisibility poset.
Prove the second Bonferroni inequality: |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| ≥ Σ|Sᵢ| - Σ|Sᵢ∩Sⱼ|, and characterize when the bound is tight (disjoint families).

sections.title: Header and Imports
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib.Combinatorics.Enumerative.InclusionExclusion and establishes the variable context. Documents the 8-part structure: general formula, inductive step, base cases, 2/3-set specializations, Bonferroni, complementary counting, 4-set case, concrete examples.

sections.title: Part I: The General Formula
sections.summary: Wraps Mathlib's inclusion_exclusion_card_biUnion into general_inclusion_exclusion: (↑|⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| : ℤ) = Σ_{∅≠t⊆s} (-1)^(|t|+1) * ↑|⋂_{i∈t} Sᵢ|. The alternating sum ranges over all nonempty subsets of the index set.

sections.title: Part II: Inductive Step
sections.summary: Proves biUnion_inter_right (distributivity of ∩ over ⋃) and card_biUnion_insert (inductive step: |⋃_{i∈insert j s} Sᵢ| = |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| + |Sⱼ| - |⋃_{i∈s}(Sᵢ∩Sⱼ)|). These are the building blocks for an inductive proof of IE.

sections.title: Part III: Base Cases
sections.summary: Proves card_biUnion_empty (empty index set gives union of cardinality 0) and card_biUnion_singleton (singleton index gives cardinality of that set). These check the formula degenerates correctly.

sections.title: Parts IV: 2-Set and 3-Set Specializations
sections.summary: Proves two_set_from_general (|A∪B|=|A|+|B|-|A∩B| in ℤ) and three_set_from_general (full 3-set IE). The three-set case requires distributivity: (A∪B)∩C=(A∩C)∪(B∩C), proved by ext+simp+tauto.

sections.title: Part V: Bonferroni Inequalities
sections.summary: Proves union_bound (first Bonferroni: |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| ≤ Σ_{i∈s}|Sᵢ|) by induction using card_union_le, and union_lower_bound (|A∪B| ≥ max(|A|,|B|)). The union bound is also known as Boole's inequality.

sections.title: Part VI: Complementary Counting
sections.summary: Proves card_sdiff_biUnion_int (|U \ ⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| = |U| - |⋃_{i∈s} Sᵢ| in ℤ) and card_complement_two (|U\(A∪B)| = |U|-|A|-|B|+|A∩B|). This is the form of IE used in sieve methods.

sections.title: Parts VII–VIII: Four-Set Formula and Examples
sections.summary: Proves four_set_inclusion_exclusion by composing the three-set and two-set formulas with four intersection distributivity steps, closed by linarith. Includes three concrete examples verified by native_decide.
